title: Improve dedicated autoscaler: burst controls + utilization reporting enhancement
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally spike above configured burst capacity during load bursts, causing unfair scaling and noisy utilization metrics. This change adds smoother burst controls to the dedicated autoscaler token-bucket, tightens throughput guarantees under steady state, and improves utilization reporting to better attribute burst vs steady traffic.

Summary of changes: - Implement token-bucket smoothing window and adaptive refill rate to reduce oscillation when short bursts hit capacity. - Add per-fleet burst attribution metrics (burst_tokens_used, burst_window_seconds) and expose them to telemetry/exporter. - Update dedicated-fleet autoscaler to prefer short-lived burst credits before triggering expensive node scale-up; adds a configurable burst_priority flag. - Emit more detailed utilization breakdowns (steady_qps, burst_qps, backlog_seconds) into the fleet utilization report. - Add integration tests for burst behavior and update docs.

Checklist: - [x] Core algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] Integration tests covering burst vs steady scenarios - [x] Metrics emitted and wired to exporter - [x] Docs and release notes updated - [x] Load-tested on staging fleet

Behavioral notes: - Default smoothing window is 30s and conservative refill factors chosen to avoid SLO regressions. Operators can tune via fleet autoscaler config (burst_window_seconds, burst_refill_factor, burst_priority). - This is backward-compatible: configs that omit burst_* fields use legacy behavior.

Related: linear ENG-3261 for autoscaler design doc, ENG-3304 for telemetry schema. This PR focuses on runtime/autoscaler and reporting; follow-ups will add UI controls in the Console and additional rollout canaries for customer fleets.

release_notes: Improve autoscaler burst handling and utilization reporting. Adds token-bucket smoothing, new burst attribution metrics, and config knobs (burst_window_seconds, burst_refill_factor, burst_priority). Backwards-compatible defaults. Recommended: monitor burst_tokens_used metric after rollout.
notes_for_ops: Default rollout on staging for 48h and monitor metrics: fleet.autoscaler.burst_tokens_used, fleet.utilization.backlog_seconds, fleet.utilization.steady_qps
If customers see increased backlog_seconds, reduce burst_refill_factor or lower burst_window_seconds to tighten burst acceptance.
This PR adds no breaking API changes; telemetry includes additional optional fields.
